sections.title: Posterior predictive discrepancies and reference distributions

missing_pieces.duty: MP-0: the handbook does not state the exact Dirichlet prior parameter vectors used for the two-class infant-temperament check (class proportions and each within-class multinomial block). It also does not reproduce the selected mixture simulation from that prior (D_min reference: mean 23.4, variance 45.3, upper tail 0.93; realized-discrepancy tail 0.74 from 500 draws). GMS 1996 sec. 3.3, p.752 describes the prior only in words and refers to Rubin, D. B. and Stern, H. S. (1994), 'Testing in latent class models using a posterior predictive check distribution', in von Eye and Clogg (eds.), Latent Variables Analysis: Applications for Developmental Research, pp. 420-438. That source is not held.

sections.title: Relative model preference versus adequacy for the intended inference

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-bayesian-model-comparison-C003 (partial): The construction or argument and the full treatment promised by the declared status (proved=annex:p15.model-density-invariance) are missing for one stated case. At body lines 136-137 of handbook/parts/p15/bayesian-model-comparison.tex, the theorem asserts that declaring a new flat prior in new parameter coordinates is not, in general, a transport of the prior. annex:p15.model-density-invariance (handbook/annex/p15/bayesian-model-comparison.tex lines 97-104) proves only that m_k is invariant under the stated transport. It then disclaims the other case without a counterexample or argument. The chapter also gives no worked boundary for the coordinate part; the null-point example at body lines 148-155 covers only density versions. The failure condition 'Missing promised direction/case' therefore holds. A related uniform-theta versus uniform-theta^2 example exists in thm:p15-bayes-transformation (bayesian-updating-prediction.tex lines 314-319), but neither this theorem nor its proof cites it, and it concerns posterior means rather than the marginal likelihood m_k.

source_presentations.extent_rule: Only the specifically selected presentation/components recorded by these source notes and locators; a reference does not add an entire monograph.

required_components.description: Distinguish prediction, comparison and model criticism.
required_components.success_condition: Use existing posterior kernels while defining the new discrepancy target.
required_components.failure_condition: Treat a Bayes factor winner as evidence of adequate absolute fit.

required_components.description: Construct posterior predictive discrepancies and reference probabilities.
required_components.success_condition: Derive the joint replicated-data/parameter construction and its computation.
required_components.failure_condition: Use an unspecified replication law or treat a posterior predictive p-value as uniformly calibrated without proof.

required_components.description: Preserve prior, posterior and mixed replication alternatives.
required_components.success_condition: Explain exactly what is held fixed in a hierarchical or auxiliary-conditioned replication.
required_components.failure_condition: Swap reference distributions without changing the interpretation.

required_components.description: Work an informative and an uninformative discrepancy.
required_components.success_condition: Show why a model may reproduce a mean while missing tails or dependence.
required_components.failure_condition: Interpret failure to detect a defect as proof of correctness.
